title: How to Fix "Margin Too Small" Errors on Amazon KDP
description: Learn exactly why Amazon KDP shows a margin too small error, how to find the object causing it, and how to fix trim size, bleed, safe area, gutter, page number, Canva, and InDesign problems before re-uploading.
metaTitle: KDP Margin Too Small Error: How to Fix It
metaDescription: Fix Amazon KDP margin too small errors with a practical checklist for trim size, PDF dimensions, bleed, safe area, gutter margins, page numbers, Canva, and InDesign exports.

excerpt: KDP's margin too small warning usually means text, page numbers, borders, or artwork are too close to the trim edge or gutter. This guide shows you how to identify the cause, fix the source file, and prevent repeat upload failures.

shortAnswer: A KDP margin too small error means that text, page numbers, borders, artwork, or another printable object is too close to the trim edge, safe-area boundary, or gutter. Fix it by verifying the trim size and PDF dimensions, moving important content inward, adding enough gutter for the page count, correcting bleed setup, exporting a fresh print PDF, and re-uploading the corrected file.

faqs.question: What does KDP margin too small mean?
faqs.answer: It means KDP found printable content too close to an edge, trim line, safe-area boundary, or gutter. The object might be body text, a page number, a header, a decorative line, a border, artwork, or a hidden element in the PDF. KDP is warning that the printed and trimmed book may cut off the object or make it look uncomfortably close to the page edge.

faqs.question: Why does my PDF look fine but KDP says the margin is too small?
faqs.answer: Most PDF viewers show the file digitally, not as a physically printed and trimmed book. KDP checks the PDF page box, trim size, bleed setting, binding side, and printable content placement. A page number that looks acceptable on a laptop screen may be only a few millimeters from the trim edge in print. Canva and Preview also may not flag hidden objects, incorrect page dimensions, or gutter problems.

faqs.question: How do I find which page is causing a KDP margin error?
faqs.answer: Open KDP Previewer and look for the highlighted page or warning detail. Then inspect that same page in the exported PDF at 100% zoom. Check the outside edge, bottom edge, header area, page number, border, and gutter side. If the warning does not name the exact object, duplicate the page, remove suspected edge elements one at a time in the source file, export a test PDF, and upload again to isolate the cause.

faqs.question: Can page numbers cause a margin too small error?
faqs.answer: Yes. Page numbers are one of the most common causes, especially when they sit low in the footer or too close to the outside page edge. Move page numbers upward and inward. For interiors, make sure odd and even pages mirror correctly so numbers do not drift toward the binding or trim edge. Re-export the PDF after adjusting the footer position.

faqs.question: Is a margin too small error the same as a bleed error?
faqs.answer: No. A margin error means important content is too close to an edge or gutter. A bleed error means artwork that should reach the edge has not extended past the trim line, or the file dimensions do not match the selected bleed setting. They are related because both involve edges, but the fix is different: move important content inward for margins; extend background artwork outward for bleed.

faqs.question: How much gutter margin do I need for KDP?
faqs.answer: The required gutter depends on page count and book format. As page count increases, the binding area hides more of the inner page, so the gutter must get wider. Do not use the same inner margin for a 60-page book and a 450-page book. Use KDP's current margin requirements for your format, then add extra space when the book is thick or the interior has charts, puzzles, or workbook content near the spine.

faqs.question: Can Canva fix KDP margin too small errors?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you fix the source design rather than only changing the export. Set the Canva file to the correct trim or full-wrap dimensions, show rulers and guides, move page numbers, headers, borders, and text inside the safe area, then export as PDF Print. Canva's canvas can look correct while the exported PDF still has edge content, so always inspect the final PDF before uploading.

faqs.question: Can I ignore a KDP margin warning?
faqs.answer: You should not ignore it unless you are certain the flagged object is expendable background artwork and the printed result will still be acceptable. For text, page numbers, borders, puzzle grids, and line art, fix the warning. KDP may let some warnings through, but the physical proof can still show cut-off text, crowded page numbers, or content disappearing into the gutter.

summary: A KDP margin too small error usually comes from text, page numbers, headers, borders, artwork, or hidden objects sitting too close to trim or gutter.
The fastest fix is to verify trim size and PDF dimensions first, then move important content inward, correct bleed settings, and re-export a fresh print PDF.
Canva, InDesign, Preview, and Acrobat can all show a file that looks fine on screen; KDP is checking print production rules, not only visual appearance.
checklist: Trim size in the source file matches the trim size selected in KDP.
Exported PDF dimensions match the selected trim and bleed setting.
Body text, headers, footers, and page numbers are inside the safe area.
Page numbers are not too low or too close to the outside edge.
Interior gutter margin is wide enough for the page count.
Decorative borders, puzzle grids, and line art do not sit beside trim.
Full-page artwork uses bleed only when artwork is extended past trim.
Hidden layers, stray objects, and template marks are removed before export.
The PDF was exported with print settings and no scaling.
The corrected PDF was checked before re-uploading to KDP.

steps.name: Verify trim size
steps.text: Confirm that the trim size selected in KDP matches the source document and exported PDF page dimensions.

steps.name: Check bleed setting
steps.text: Confirm whether the book is uploaded as bleed or no bleed, then make sure the PDF dimensions and artwork extension match that choice.

steps.name: Inspect flagged pages
steps.text: Open the warning pages in KDP Previewer and the final PDF. Check text, page numbers, headers, footers, borders, images, and hidden objects near all edges.

steps.name: Fix safe area and gutter
steps.text: Move important content inward, raise low page numbers, and increase gutter margin for thicker books or content near the spine.

content: You upload your manuscript or cover to Amazon KDP. The PDF looks clean. Canva did not complain. Adobe Acrobat opens it without any obvious problem. Then KDP Previewer stops you with a warning: **Margin Too Small**.
This is frustrating because the file often looks fine on screen. Nothing appears cut off. The page seems centered. You export again, upload again, and KDP shows the same warning again.

The reason is simple: KDP is not only checking whether the PDF opens. It is checking whether the file can survive physical printing, binding, and trimming. A book page is not a digital rectangle. It is printed on paper, cut down to size, and bound. That process needs extra space around important content.

A KDP margin too small error usually means one of three things: the PDF is the wrong size, important content is too close to the trim edge, or the gutter is too narrow for the book's binding. Sometimes the cause is a visible object like a page number. Sometimes it is a stray line, template mark, hidden layer, or border you forgot was still in the file.

This guide walks through the exact checks to make, the most common causes, and the fixes in Canva and InDesign. The goal is not to trick KDP Previewer into accepting the file. The goal is to fix the source PDF so the printed book looks right.
## Quick Fix Checklist
Before digging into individual pages, run through this checklist. It catches most margin too small errors quickly.
- Verify the trim size selected in KDP.
- Verify the exported PDF page dimensions.
- Check whether the project is bleed or no bleed.
- Keep text, page numbers, headers, footers, and logos inside the safe area.
- Check the gutter margin on the binding side.
- Move page numbers upward and inward if they sit near the bottom edge.
- Remove hidden objects, template marks, and stray lines near trim.
- Re-export as a print PDF without scaling.
- Re-upload the corrected PDF to KDP Previewer.

If you want a fast second pass before uploading, run the final file through [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker). It can check dimensions, bleed, safe areas, spine setup, and print-readiness before KDP catches the same issue.
## What "Margin Too Small" Actually Means

A margin is the empty or protected space between important content and a page edge. On KDP, the margin is not just a design preference. It protects text and graphics from trimming variation and binding loss.

The trim line is the final cut edge of the printed page. Anything too close to this edge can look crowded or be partially cut off after printing. The safe area is the inward zone where important content should live. Bleed is the opposite: it is extra background artwork that extends outward past trim so edge-to-edge art does not leave a white sliver.

The gutter is the inside margin near the book's binding. It matters more as page count increases. A 60-page paperback can open flatter than a 500-page paperback. Thick books need more inner margin because the spine curve hides content near the binding.
| Term | What it means | What goes there | Common mistake |
| Margin | Protected empty space inside the page | Nothing important | Treating it like optional decoration space |
| Safe area | Interior zone safe from trim variation | Text, page numbers, logos, key art | Placing small text outside it |
| Trim line | Final intended cut edge | No important content | Designing right up to it |
| Bleed | Extra artwork beyond trim | Background color, patterns, edge art | Putting text in bleed |
| Gutter | Binding-side margin | Extra blank space | Using the same inner margin for every page count |
| Printable area | Region KDP can print reliably | Designed content | Assuming screen preview equals print safety |
The rule is easy to remember: important content moves inward; expendable background art extends outward.
## Margin Error vs Safe Area Error vs Bleed Error
Creators often confuse margin, safe area, and bleed because all three involve edges. But the warning tells you which direction the fix should move.

A margin error usually means content is too close to the page edge or gutter. A safe-area warning means important content is outside the protected zone. A bleed error means artwork that should reach the edge has not been extended beyond trim, or the PDF dimensions do not match the bleed setting.
| Warning type | Usually caused by | Fix direction | Example |
| Margin too small | Text, page number, border, grid, header, footer too close | Move content inward | Page number sits too low |
| Safe area issue | Important object outside protected zone | Move object inward | Subtitle touches cover trim risk zone |
| Bleed issue | Edge artwork or background stops at trim | Extend background outward | Black page has white edge after trimming |

Real example: if a coloring page has a decorative border 0.05 inches from the edge, that is a margin or safe-area risk. If the black background of that page stops exactly at the trim line, that is a bleed problem. If the page was exported at the wrong size, KDP may show either kind of warning because all measurements are now based on the wrong page geometry.
For a deeper edge-art comparison, see [KDP Bleed vs No Bleed](/blog/kdp-bleed-vs-no-bleed). For cover-specific protected zones, see [KDP Safe Area Explained](/blog/kdp-safe-area-explained).
## 13 Reasons KDP Shows a Margin Too Small Error
### 1. Wrong Trim Size
What it is: the trim size selected in KDP does not match the document you designed. A file built as 8.5 x 11 will not validate correctly if KDP is set to 6 x 9.
Why it happens: creators duplicate old templates, use a Canva preset, or change trim size late in the upload flow.
How to detect it: compare the source document size, exported PDF page size, and KDP trim selection.
How to fix it: set all three to the same trim size, then reflow the layout. Do not simply scale the PDF down if text and margins become too tight.
### 2. Wrong PDF Dimensions
What it is: the exported PDF page box does not match the trim and bleed setting KDP expects.
Why it happens: export scaling, printer marks, wrong artboard size, or a front-cover-only canvas used for a full wrap.
How to detect it: open PDF properties in Acrobat or Preview and check the page size.
How to fix it: export from the correct document size with no scaling and no extra crop marks unless your workflow specifically requires them.
### 3. Text Too Close to Edge
What it is: body text, captions, labels, or callouts sit near the outside trim edge.
Why it happens: the page looks balanced on screen, but print margins are measured in inches or millimeters, not vibes.
How to detect it: inspect every edge at 100% zoom and compare against your margin guides.
How to fix it: move text inward or reduce the text box width so it does not approach the edge.
### 4. Page Numbers Too Low
What it is: footer page numbers sit close to the bottom trim line.
Why it happens: templates often place page numbers visually low because they look elegant in digital previews.
How to detect it: check pages with page numbers, especially front matter and chapter openers.
How to fix it: raise page numbers and keep them inside the safe area on both odd and even pages.
### 5. Headers Too Close to Trim
What it is: running headers, chapter titles, or author names sit too close to the top edge.
Why it happens: header spacing is often copied from documents intended for digital reading or home printing.
How to detect it: inspect the top margin on regular pages and chapter pages.
How to fix it: lower the header or increase the top margin in the source file.
### 6. Decorative Borders Too Close
What it is: a frame, rule, or decorative box sits near the trim line.
Why it happens: borders look attractive in templates but reveal tiny print shifts immediately.
How to detect it: look for thin lines near the page edge, especially in journals, planners, and coloring books.
How to fix it: move borders inward, thicken them, make them partial, or remove them.
### 7. Full-Page Artwork Without Bleed
What it is: artwork reaches the page edge but the file does not include bleed.
Why it happens: the design is made at trim size and uploaded as if edge-to-edge printing will still work.
How to detect it: artwork touches the edge of the PDF page and KDP is set to no bleed, or the bleed-sized page lacks extended artwork.
How to fix it: use a bleed document and extend background art past trim. Keep text inward.
### 8. Wrong Bleed Setup
What it is: the selected KDP bleed option and PDF dimensions disagree.
Why it happens: users enable bleed in KDP but export a trim-size PDF, or export bleed but choose no bleed.
How to detect it: compare PDF dimensions with KDP's expected dimensions for that trim size and bleed choice.
How to fix it: make the source file, export, and KDP setting agree.
### 9. Small Gutter Margin
What it is: content is too close to the binding side of the page.
Why it happens: the layout uses symmetrical margins even though bound books need extra inner space.
How to detect it: check the inner side of odd and even pages. In a paperback, the inner edge alternates left and right.
How to fix it: increase the inside margin or gutter setting, then re-export the full manuscript.
### 10. High Page Count With Narrow Gutter
What it is: the book is thick enough that the binding eats more interior space than expected.
Why it happens: the manuscript grows after formatting, but the margins are never updated.
How to detect it: compare page count against KDP's current minimum margin guidance and inspect pages near the spine.
How to fix it: increase gutter margin and review text reflow. Thick workbooks often need more than the bare minimum.
### 11. Canva Export Issue
What it is: the Canva design looks correct, but the exported PDF dimensions or object placement are wrong.
Why it happens: wrong custom size, Standard PDF export, accidental resizing, or missing guide setup.
How to detect it: check the exported PDF properties and inspect the PDF itself, not just the Canva canvas.
How to fix it: set exact dimensions, use guides, export as PDF Print, and verify the final PDF.
### 12. Hidden Layers Near Edge
What it is: an invisible or nearly invisible object remains near the trim edge.
Why it happens: templates, guide marks, old text boxes, transparent shapes, and pasted objects can remain in the file.
How to detect it: use the object/layers panel in your design app, or select all objects on the problem page.
How to fix it: delete hidden objects and template marks before export.
### 13. Cover and Interior Mismatch
What it is: cover and interior choices disagree on trim size, page count, spine width, or bleed assumptions.
Why it happens: the cover was designed before the manuscript page count was final.
How to detect it: compare the interior trim size, cover template, page count, paper type, and full-wrap PDF size.

How to fix it: finalize the manuscript first, then rebuild the cover from the correct KDP template. The related guide [Why Amazon KDP Says Cover Size Does Not Match Interior](/blog/kdp-cover-size-does-not-match-interior) covers this in detail.
## How to Check Your PDF Properly
Do not rely only on the design app. KDP reads the exported PDF. Your checks should happen on that final exported file.

**Adobe Acrobat:** open File Properties and confirm the page size. Use rulers or measurement tools to check the distance from text, borders, and page numbers to the page edge. Acrobat is especially useful for spotting wrong PDF dimensions.

**Mac Preview:** open the PDF, show thumbnails, and scan the page edges. Preview is not a full preflight tool, but it is useful for quickly spotting low page numbers, stray border lines, and wrong page orientation.
**Canva:** use rulers, guides, and the KDP template as visual helpers, but remember Canva is the source view. Export and inspect the PDF separately.

**KDP Previewer:** treat it as the final production simulation. When it flags a page, do not keep re-exporting randomly. Go back to the source page, identify the edge object, fix it, and upload a new PDF.

Recommended screenshots for your own troubleshooting notes: PDF properties showing page dimensions, the KDP Previewer warning page, a close-up of the suspected object, and the source-file guide setup.
## How to Fix Margin Errors in Canva
Start with the original Canva file. Do not try to repair the exported PDF manually unless you have no source file.

1. Open the design and confirm the custom document size. For interiors, it should match the trim size plus bleed only when bleed is used. For covers, it should be the full wrap size, not only the front cover.
2. Turn on rulers and guides. Add guides for trim, safe area, and gutter. If you are designing a cover, place the official KDP template as a locked guide layer.
3. Find the flagged page or cover area. Check page numbers, headers, borders, bottom labels, puzzle grids, and decorative objects first.
4. Move content inward. Use Canva's position controls when possible instead of dragging by eye.
5. Raise low page numbers. Page numbers should not sit near the bottom trim edge.
6. Check bleed. If artwork reaches the edge, extend the background beyond the trim guide. Do not move text into bleed.
7. Remove hidden or unused objects. Select suspicious areas near edges and delete old marks or template residue.
8. Export as PDF Print. Avoid Standard PDF for KDP print files.
9. Open the exported PDF and check dimensions before uploading.
If Canva is producing the wrong full-wrap cover dimensions, compare your setup with [KDP Cover Dimensions Not Matching Template](/blog/kdp-cover-dimensions-not-matching-template).
## How to Fix Margin Errors in Adobe InDesign
InDesign is precise, but it will still export a bad KDP file if the document setup is wrong.
1. Open Document Setup and confirm trim size, facing pages, and bleed. Interior pages with no edge-to-edge artwork usually do not need bleed. Edge artwork does.
2. Open Margins and Columns. Set top, bottom, outside, and inside margins intentionally. The inside margin should account for gutter and page count.
3. Check parent pages. Headers, footers, page numbers, and running elements often live on parent pages, so one bad parent can affect the whole manuscript.
4. Use Preflight. InDesign's preflight panel can catch overset text and missing assets, while your own margin guides catch KDP edge risks.
5. Inspect problem pages. Look for objects sitting outside the page, transparent shapes, old template marks, and footers near trim.
6. Export with Adobe PDF Print. Use no scaling, include bleed only when required, and avoid printer marks unless you know they belong in your KDP workflow.
7. Open the exported PDF and verify page dimensions in Acrobat.

The most common InDesign mistake is fixing the visible page but forgetting a parent-page footer or page-number frame. If page numbers are the cause, update the parent page and inspect both left and right pages.
## Special Case: Coloring Books
Coloring books often trigger margin warnings because they use borders, line art, puzzle grids, mandalas, and activity layouts near the edge.

A coloring page can fail even if there is no body text. KDP still sees printable content. A thin border close to trim is just as risky as a sentence close to trim. A maze wall, dot-to-dot number, or puzzle clue near the edge can be flagged too.
For coloring books, use these habits:
- Keep decorative borders well inside the safe area.
- Do not place page numbers low beside the trim edge.
- Keep puzzle grids and activity instructions away from the gutter.
- Use bleed only when the artwork is meant to reach the physical edge.
- Add extra inner margin for thick activity books.

Low-content and activity books repeat the same layout across many pages, so a single margin mistake can appear hundreds of times. Fix the master page, template, or duplicated source layout before exporting again.
## Special Case: Gutter Margin Problems
Gutter errors are easy to miss because the page can look centered as a single PDF page. But bound books have an inside edge. Some of that inside edge disappears into the spine curve.

The thicker the book, the more important the gutter becomes. A journal with 100 pages and a workbook with 480 pages should not use identical inner margins. In thick books, text near the spine can become hard to read even if KDP technically accepts the file.

Check gutter problems by viewing pages as spreads. Odd pages and even pages should mirror correctly. The inner margin should alternate. If every page has the same left and right margin, your layout may not be accounting for binding.

Fix gutter problems in the source document. Increasing the inside margin will reflow text, change page count, and possibly affect cover spine width. That is normal. Recalculate the cover after the manuscript page count changes. For spine-specific cover issues, see [KDP Spine Width Wrong](/blog/kdp-spine-width-wrong).
## Cover Margin Problems
KDP margin warnings are not limited to interiors. Covers can have unsafe text, barcode conflicts, spine problems, and trim-edge risks.

On the front cover, titles, subtitles, badges, and author names should stay inside the safe area. On the back cover, blurbs and logos need room from trim and the barcode zone. On the spine, text must fit inside the actual spine width and stay away from fold edges.

A cover built from the wrong template can create multiple warnings at once. The title may be too close to trim, the spine text may overflow, and the barcode area may conflict with back-cover text. Fix the template first. Then fix individual elements.
For cover-safe checks before exporting, use [How to Check Safe Area Before Exporting Your KDP Cover](/blog/how-to-check-safe-area-before-exporting-kdp-cover).
## Manual Troubleshooting Workflow
When the warning is unclear, use a structured sequence instead of guessing.

Start with the KDP margin error. Check page size first. If the page size is wrong, fix the document and export again. If the page size is right, compare the trim size selected in KDP. If trim size is right, check bleed. If bleed is right, inspect safe area. If safe area is clean, check gutter. If gutter is clean, inspect for hidden objects. Then re-export and upload again.
In short:
1. Margin error.
2. Page size.
3. Trim size.
4. Bleed setting.
5. Safe area.
6. Gutter.
7. Hidden objects.
8. Re-export.
9. Upload again.
This order matters because a wrong page size makes every other measurement unreliable.
## How KDPPreflight Helps
KDPPreflight is useful before upload because it checks the file as a production PDF, not just as a pretty design preview.

It can help identify trim-size mismatches, bleed setup problems, safe-area risks, spine width problems, and PDF readiness issues. That does not guarantee Amazon approval, because KDP is the final validator and Amazon can update requirements. But it gives you a practical pre-upload pass so you can fix obvious issues before spending another upload cycle in KDP Previewer.
Use it after exporting the final PDF, not halfway through the design. The final PDF is the file KDP will analyze.
## Common Mistakes
**Re-uploading the same file repeatedly.** If KDP flagged the PDF, uploading it again will not change the geometry. Fix the source file.
**Changing the KDP trim size to make the warning disappear.** This creates a different mismatch. The trim size should match the book you actually designed.
**Assuming PDF Print fixes margins.** Export settings preserve quality and dimensions, but they do not move unsafe content inward.
**Forgetting mirrored pages.** Odd and even pages have different inside edges. Check both.
**Using border-heavy templates.** Thin edge borders are fragile in print and frequently trigger warnings.
**Ignoring page count changes.** More pages can require a wider gutter and a wider cover spine.
**Leaving template marks visible.** Delete or hide guide layers before export unless they are truly non-printing.
**Checking the Canva canvas but not the PDF.** KDP reads the exported PDF.
## Final Pre-Upload Checklist
Use this final checklist before approving KDP Previewer.
- The manuscript trim size matches the KDP selection.
- The cover template matches trim size, page count, paper type, and bleed.
- PDF dimensions are correct in document properties.
- No scaling was applied during export.
- Body text stays inside interior margins.
- Page numbers are safely above the bottom trim edge.
- Headers are not too close to the top trim edge.
- Gutter is wide enough for the page count.
- Borders, frames, line art, and puzzle grids are inside safe margins.
- Edge-to-edge artwork has real bleed.
- Text is never placed in bleed.
- Hidden layers and template marks are removed.
- The final exported PDF has been checked, not only the source file.
- KDP Previewer has been reviewed page by page for warnings.
## Conclusion
A KDP margin too small error is not random. It is KDP telling you that something in the PDF is too close to a physical production boundary: trim, safe area, or gutter.

The fix is usually straightforward once you stop guessing. Verify trim size. Verify PDF dimensions. Check bleed. Move important content inward. Increase gutter when the page count requires it. Re-export from the source file and upload the corrected PDF.
The creators who get stuck are usually re-uploading the same broken geometry. The creators who fix it quickly identify the object that triggered the warning and correct the file before trying again.
Before your next upload, run the final PDF through [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) so you can catch margin, safe-area, bleed, spine, and PDF readiness problems before Amazon KDP does.
